summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis and chronic abdominal pain was admitted with acute epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had a gastroparesis flare, with labs showing only mild lipase elevation, ruling out acute pancreatitis. Metoclopramide was avoided due to interaction risks with her venlafaxine. She was started on IV erythromycin, which improved her symptoms, allowing advancement to a regular diet. She was transitioned to oral erythromycin and discharged home in stable condition after six days. Follow-up was arranged with her primary care physician and gastroenterologist. Her anxiety, depression, and hearing impairment were acknowledged and accommodated throughout the stay.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
